newsitem.title: CANADA: Northrock in conditional oil asset sale.
newsitem.headline: Northrock in conditional oil asset sale.

text.p: Northrock Resources Ltd said on Monday it agreed to sell non-strategic oil and natural gas properties for proceeds of about C$45 million.
Northrock said the deal was contingent on the purchaser, which was not disclosed, completing the initial public offering of a royalty trust. The IPO was exected to close on March 1.
The company said it would use the proceeds to reduce bank debt, which would give it flexibility to pursue additional exploration development and acquisition opportunities.
Based on a capital program of C$76 million, debt at December 31, 1997 was anticipated to be less than 1.5 times 1998 cash flow, Northrock said.
It said the properties being sold were mature, had long-life reserves and offered Northrock limited exploration and development upside.

The impact from the sale on the company's 1997 production volumes was expected to be 1,600 barrels of oil equivalent per day and exploration and development in the first quarter of 1997 was projected to fully replace the output loss, Northrock said.
It said its 1996 exit production rate was over 11,500 BOED.
